Since D027 is the only 2025 disclosure containing this evidence, it is the counterpart.

comparisons.peer_topic: RF semiconductor devices and FBAR technology
comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom offers RF semiconductor devices using proprietary FBAR technology to filter and amplify signals, holding a significant market share in cellular handsets.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Broadcom (AVGO) focus on the internal or proprietary development of RF filter technologies (FBAR for AVGO, RFFE modules/filters for QCOM) which are critical components of front-end modules. While AVGO highlights its proprietary FBAR technology's market share, QCOM specifies that it uses internal fabrication facilities for certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, indicating a vertical integration strategy for these specific RF components similar to AVGO's technology advantage, rather than a fully fabless approach for these parts.

sentences.text: QCT primarily uses internal fabrication facilities to manufacture certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, and our manufacturing operations consist of front-end and back-end processes.

• RF Semiconductor Devices: Our RF semiconductor devices selectively filter, as well as amplify and route, RF signals. Filters enable modern wireless communication systems to support a large number of subscribers simultaneously by ensuring that the multiple transmissions and receptions of voice and data streams do not interfere with each other. We were among the first to deliver commercial film bulk acoustic resonator ("FBAR") filters that offer technological advantages over competing filter technologies, to allow mobile handsets to function more efficiently in today's congested RF spectrum. FBAR technology has a significant market share within the cellular handset market. Our RF products include multi-chip module front-end modules that integrate transmit/receive switching and filtering functions for multiple frequency bands, filter modules and discrete filters, all using our proprietary FBAR technology.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company has a long history of operating in Asia, where it manufactures and sources the majority of its products and materials, and stores the majority of its product inventory in a warehouse in Malaysia.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies operate manufacturing or sourcing facilities in Asia, specifically Singapore and/or Malaysia. QCOM places its back-end assembly, packaging, and test facilities in China and Singapore, while AVGO manufactures and sources the majority of its products in Asia, with inventory stored in a warehouse in Malaysia. This highlights a shared geographic reliance on Asian infrastructure for back-end processing and supply chain proximity.

We also have a long history of operating in Asia where we manufacture and source the majority of our products and materials.
We store the majority of our product inventory in our warehouse in Malaysia and our presence in Asia places us in close proximity to many of our customers' manufacturing facilities.

peer_results.rationale: Intel's disclosures describe a comprehensive integrated device manufacturer (IDM) model with extensive global wafer fabrication and assembly/test facilities, including specific expansion projects in Ireland, Arizona, and Ohio. QCOM is primarily fabless with internal facilities only for specific RFFE modules. Intel's disclosure does not mention internal fabrication for specific module components like QCOM's RFFE focus, nor does it describe the same hybrid/fabless-with-exceptions strategy.

comparisons.peer_topic: Manufacturing strategy and centers of excellence
comparisons.peer_summary: The company manufactures products at wholly-owned facilities and uses subcontractors for certain processes, leveraging a global network of centers of excellence that integrate fabrication and back-end manufacturing to provide efficient support structures and quicker cycle times.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Micron (MU) utilize a hybrid manufacturing model involving both wholly-owned/internal facilities and subcontractors, with a specific integration of fabrication and back-end processes. QCOM uses internal facilities for RFFE front-end and back-end in Singapore, while MU explicitly states that its centers of excellence bring fabrication and back-end manufacturing together, particularly in Singapore and Taiwan. Both leverage this integrated structure for efficiency.

sentences.text: QCT primarily uses internal fabrication facilities to manufacture certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, and our manufacturing operations consist of front-end and back-end processes.
Our back-end manufacturing facilities are located in China and Singapore.
We manufacture our products at wholly-owned facilities and also utilize subcontractors for certain manufacturing processes.
For our locations in Singapore and Taiwan, this is also a combination of bringing fabrication and back-end manufacturing together.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global manufacturing footprint and subcontractor use
comparisons.peer_summary: Products are manufactured in own facilities across seven countries and utilize subcontractors for certain processes.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Micron (MU) explicitly list Singapore as a key location for their manufacturing operations. QCOM identifies Singapore as a site for both front-end (wafer fabrication) and back-end (assembly, packaging, and test) processes, while MU lists Singapore as one of the locations where products are manufactured in its own facilities.

sentences.text: The front-end processes primarily take place at manufacturing facilities located in Germany and Singapore and involve the imprinting of substrate wafers with the structure and circuitry required for the products to function (also known as wafer fabrication).
Our back-end manufacturing facilities are located in China and Singapore.

We manufacture our products within our own facilities located in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, the United States, Malaysia, China, and India and also utilize subcontractors to perform certain manufacturing processes.

peer_results.rationale: NVIDIA is described as utilizing a pure fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, relying entirely on key suppliers for all phases including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging to avoid owning manufacturing operations. This is fundamentally different from QCOM, which uses internal fabrication facilities for certain RFFE modules and RF filter products. NVDA's disclosure explicitly contrasts with QCOM's partial internal fabrication capability.
